terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: The one module of the outdoor roof kit carried on a SINGLE CENTRE POLE: a 4 x 4 m square canvas canopy on the same 4 m grid as the four-post bays, so placed side by side the canopies meet at their edges and the pole lands mid-bay. A real umbrella cranks open and tilts, but the asset declares no mechanism, so one root pivot and zero sockets. Cafe terraces, hotel pools, temple fairs: the big square shade umbrella. Cream canvas gone grey along every seam, a yellowed sun side, a runner collar on a chipped cream pole, a galvanised cast base with a boss.

reasoning: ONE canvas merge -- the hipped canopy on 48 perimeter samples and seven rings, the crown cap with its skirt, the valance and four corner tabs -- and ONE metal merge -- base, boss, spigot, pole, runner, hub, finial, eight ribs and eight struts: TWO draw calls of 4.

Two materials of three: the canvas (vertex colours for the top, the shaded valance and the cap, under ONE 1024 px dirt canvas mapped in PLAN with a valance strip along its bottom) and the metal (vertex colours: painted cream pole and runner, bare steel spigot, galvanised base, ribs, finial). A colour difference is not a material difference.
No repetition system: eight ribs and eight struts are one merge of 16 bars at 12 triangles each, cheaper than an InstancedMesh submission.
Action readiness: one root pivot, zero sockets, no declared collider shape, no destruction groups.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The identity is the steep square pyramid on one pole with its straight valance -- geometry -- and at prop distance the sixteen dirt-lined seams and the sag between the ribs, which are what separate a used cafe umbrella from a white slab. The seams are a canvas over modelled sag; the ribs are real bars because the player stands UNDER this prop and sees them.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 4.00 x 3.30 x 4.00 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=4000 triangles, <=4 draw calls, <=3 materials, <=6 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus 0 named mechanism pivot(s); zero sockets; none collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

pivotInventory.name: root
pivotInventory.justification: The rigid body of the prop at its declared origin. A named pivot is a promise that a part turns on it, and only real mechanisms get one.

actionReadiness.socketJustification: ZERO sockets, deliberately. Nothing attaches to this prop and nothing is emitted from it. A marker named for a place on the surface is a location, not a mechanism.
actionReadiness.destructionJustification: The asset declares destructionGroups as an empty list -- this prop is NOT breakable. No component carries actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup. promote-model checks built against declared as an equality in BOTH directions, so an invented group fails the gate just as a missing one would.

assumptions: The plate shows a pointed tab hanging at ONE corner of the valance; the build hangs one at every corner, on the symmetry of the canopy.

The plate's canvas has sixteen seams (four panels per side) but a square umbrella of this size has eight ribs (corners and mids), so the seams are dirt lines in the canvas and the sag is between the ribs.
The underside of the canopy carries the same dirt canvas as the top (the plate never shows it); the ribs and struts are what a player sees from below.
The crown cap is a small square roof over a vent, hanging 3 cm above the canopy; the plate shows it raised and skirted.

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center, +Y up, the pole on the axis. A neighbouring umbrella sits at +-4.00 m on X or Z and the two canopies meet edge to edge; the corner tabs lean 1.5 cm out from a 1.985 half-span so nothing crosses +-2.000.

silhouette.description: A 4.00 x 4.00 m square canopy: eave at 2.40, crown at 3.20, the canvas sagging 0.09 between eight radial ribs, a 0.68 m square crown cap to 3.26 with a 0.04 skirt and a finial disc to 3.30. A straight 0.30 m valance to 2.10 with a 0.16 x 0.17 pointed tab at each corner. A cream pole r 0.035 on a bare steel spigot r 0.026 to 0.42, a runner collar r 0.05 at 1.42 and a hub at 3.10; a galvanised base disc r 0.28 x 0.07 with a boss r 0.10; eight ribs and eight struts under the canvas.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x and z span exactly -2.000..+2.000 at the corner tabs (the canopy itself stops at 1.985); y 0.00 at the base to 3.30 at the finial. HEIGHT RE-DECLARED FROM THE PROXY before this build (2.80 -> 3.30, registry notes): the Meshy proxy reads the canopy at w/h 1.07 with the eave band at 0.66-0.77 H and the peak at 1.0 H -- a pyramid rising 0.23 H over a 0.535 H half-span, 23 degrees -- under which the first build's 2.10-edge / 2.80-peak canopy was a 12-degree slab. Width is the axis the grid fixes and the walk-under rim stays at 2.10, so the valance is 0.30 m to an eave at 2.40 and the canopy rises 0.80 to 3.20 under a crown cap at 3.26 and a finial at 3.30: 24 degrees. The proxy at 4 m wide would be 3.74 m tall; the remaining band-table residual (canopy 1.21 W/H against the proxy's 1.07) is that declaration. Base r 0.28 is the proxy's 0.205 H disc; mast r 0.035 its 0.012 H stem.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate: canopy w/h 1.07 with the eave band at 0.66-0.77 H and the peak at 1.0 H (radius profile, scratch/_mon/profile.mjs), stem 0.012 H, base 0.205 H wide. Used for the PITCH and the valance depth, which the first build took from the notes alone; the declared 4 m width governs the plan.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.92: the umbrella is four-fold symmetric about its pole; the plate shows one hanging corner tab and the build gives every corner one.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: A WHITE double-sided material carrying cream, the shaded valance and the cap as vertex colours, under one dirt canvas mapped in plan.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

roughness.notes: Scalar observed for this surface in the plate. The independently extracted map is kept on disk as evidence and is NOT bound at runtime -- this material is textureless, so the scalar is the runtime value.

albedo.samplingNotes: Measured as the mean of crops/canopy.png. extract_pbr_evidence confidence 0.880. The extractor palette is advisory only: these crops are flat material swatches, not isolated objects, so its foreground separation is weak by its own warnings. Albedo is the direct crop measurement.

localOverrides.region: sixteen radial seams of the canopy
localOverrides.evidence: crops/canopy.png -- every seam on the plate is a grey-brown dirt line widening toward the eave; carried as four nested strokes (34..2 px) per seam with elongated smears along it.

localOverrides.region: the valance and the cap skirt
localOverrides.evidence: crops/valance.png -- a hem seam near the bottom, a top seam under the eave, faint drips; carried in the canvas strip.

evidence: Measured on viewEvidence region-canopy (0.88) at #dfd8cb, luma 216.8 (probed 213-232 across the sunlit and shaded panels), region-valance (0.86) at #cdc4b4, luma 197, hanging in the canopy's shade. The harness lights a top face at ~1.15x, so the canopy is carried at #d4cab8 and PROBED back at luma 211-217 on the review render against the plate's 213-232.
The valance and cap are vertex colours #d4ccbc / #cfc5b2 on the same white material -- a colour difference, not a material difference.

Textureless as DECLARED: one 1024 px dirt canvas after construction, mapped in PLAN over the canopy (u = x, v = z) with the valance, cap skirt and tabs on a strip along its bottom: sixteen radial seam lines with a soft halo and smears, a warm cast on some panels, 260 downhill dust streaks, crown grime, a hem seam and drips on the valance.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

reviewHistory.summary: Structural pass: hipped canopy on 48 samples and seven rings from a 0.06 vent to the 1.985 eave, straight 0.30 valance, crown cap, pole on a spigot in a bossed base, eight ribs and eight struts from the runner.

Owner review (v3, 2026-09-03): "fix the z-fighting in the base". Probed on the shipped bundle, every cylY cap fan was wound inside out -- the base disc's top faced -Y (culled, so the boss read as an open crescent) and its bottom faced +Y at y 0, coincident and co-facing with the level ground plane. Cap winding reversed; side walls were correct.

Scalloped eave removed (the plate's hem is straight); rings 4 -> 7 and sag 0.06 -> 0.09 so the sag reads; crown cap, finial, corner tabs (first cut 0.26 x 0.30 read as wings, now 0.16 x 0.17), runner collar, spigot, bossed base, ribs and struts added; canopy half 1.985 so the tabs reach exactly 2.000.

featureReviews.evidence: Canvas sagging 0.09 between eight ribs over seven rings (the sag reads on the 0 and 315 renders as soft valleys, where the first build's four rings were flat facets); a STRAIGHT valance with a pointed tab at each corner; a 0.68 m crown cap with a skirt over the vent and a round finial; eight ribs and eight struts from a runner collar under the canvas, seen from below.
featureReviews.notes: The plate shows one corner tab; the build gives every corner one. The cap reads slightly boxier than the plate's soft one.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.92. 1,280/4,000 triangles, 2/4 draw calls, 2/3 materials, 2/6 unique geometries, one 1024 px canvas at 5.6 MB, factory ~40 ms. check-coplanar clean; every azimuth turntable-gated with the closed canopy carrying the silhouette.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the large class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Two components, no repetition system: 2 of 4.

materials.note: canvas and metal: 2 of 3. Valance and cap tones are vertex colours on the canvas; pole, spigot, base and ribs are vertex colours on the metal.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 1,280 of 4,000: ~700 in the canopy merge (7 x 48 rings, cap, valance, tabs), ~580 in the metal merge (seven cylinders, sixteen bars).

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: A sampled square-outline surface for the canopy, cap and valance; cylinders and square bars for the metal.
No InstancedMesh: sixteen 12-triangle bars merge cheaper than they instance. In a scene the HOST places whole umbrellas on the 4 m grid.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.
Both materials are declared textureless. One 1024 px canvas after construction (~5.6 MB of texture VRAM), bound as map only; factory ~40 ms.

risks.description: The proxy canopy is w/h 1.07; at the grid's 4 m width that is 3.74 m tall, and the build is 3.30 so the rim stays at 2.10.
risks.mitigation: Pitch matches the proxy (24 against 23 degrees); the residual is the declaration, recorded in the registry notes.

risks.description: The dirt canvas is mapped in plan, so the seams stretch slightly along the slope and the valance strip repeats four times.
risks.mitigation: On a 24 degree slope the stretch is 9%; the strip carries no mark that reads as repeated.

risks.description: The space between the valance and the base is background beside the pole.
risks.mitigation: It is open to the sides, not enclosed; the closed canopy carries the silhouette.
